# Pilindavaccha Sutta (Ud 3.6 (PTS Ud 28))

**ID:** Ud 3.6 (PTS Ud 28)
**Section:** Udāna (ud)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Pilindavaccha Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pilindavaccha Sutta* is the sixth discourse of the *Nandavagga*, the third chapter of the *Udāna* (Ud 3.6, PTS Ud 28) [Masefield 1997]. In this sutta, monks complain to the Buddha that the elder Pilindavaccha repeatedly addresses his fellow monastics with terms reserved for outcastes or menials (*vasalavāda*) [Masefield 1997; Jetjiravat]. The Buddha summons Pilindavaccha and inquires into his conduct, then reflects on his former existences and explains to the assembly that Pilindavaccha—despite having attained arahantship—acted entirely without malice; his manner of speaking was merely an ingrained habitual tendency (*vāsanā*) persisting from having been reborn in a brāhman family for five hundred consecutive lifetimes [Jetjiravat; Masefield 1997].

 It also notes a resembling passage in the *Pūraḷāsa Sutta* (Snp 3.4) and a mention in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1).
